description: crate-jmap-base-client/src/client.rs:673-676 uses 'std::str::from_utf8(&raw[..valid_up_to]).expect("valid_up_to is a valid UTF-8 boundary")'. The crate enforces #![forbid(unsafe_code)] (lib.rs:23) so the safer alternative — std::str::from_utf8_unchecked, which IS the legitimate use of unsafe here — is unavailable. That leaves expect() as the cheapest path. The expect message DOES carry the soundness argument ('valid_up_to is the documented prefix length that IS valid UTF-8 by construction'), so this passes the workspace rule that every expect() in production code must have a comment explaining why it cannot fail. Flagging for visibility because: (1) the unsafe-forbidden + expect-with-comment combination is the right call given the crate's policy and IS the idiomatic Rust answer to 'I have a slice I know is valid UTF-8 but the type system doesn't', (2) a future reviewer who notices the expect() without seeing the forbid(unsafe_code) ceiling may try to 'fix' it by reaching for unwrap_or_default() — which would silently drop valid UTF-8 prefix bytes on a hypothetical impossible failure path. Recommendation: no code change. Add one extra line to the SAFETY-style comment explicitly tying it to forbid(unsafe_code) so the policy connection is visible to future readers.
